I have farmed these 12.4 mu in Quzhou for 35 years, and I know what works on this land. With six people in my household and some of my family working off-farm, I need crops that give me steady returns without needing me in the fields every hour. My well gives me water when the rains fail, so I irrigate at the critical moments.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October. I sowed 10 mu with improved Jimai 22 after rotary tillage. Now that it is turning green in early spring, I will top-dress urea—about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu—because the wheat is hungry after winter and needs strength to grow tillers. I will irrigate three times: at green-up, at jointing, and at grain filling. I will spray once for weeds, twice for insects, and once for fungus if the weather turns damp. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the season is fair.

After I cut the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant summer maize on the same 10 mu. There is no time to plough between crops, so I use no-tillage direct seeding. I buy hybrid seed, Denghai 605, because it grows fast and yields well. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and top-dress urea when the maize is knee-high—about 14 kg nitrogen per mu in total. I irrigate twice during the summer if the rains are sparse, and spray herbicide once and insecticide twice. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

For cotton, I keep 2.4 mu on the side. The price is usually better than grain, though it needs more labor. I will rotary-till the cotton plot in April and plant improved seed when the soil warms. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and urea at flowering—about 10 kg nitrogen per mu total. Cotton attracts bollworm and aphids, so I spray pesticide about 12 times through the season. I irrigate twice, once at flowering and once at boll stage. I hope for 260 kg of seed cotton per mu.
